extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students and researchers of humor/comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Describing what a punch line is, how it functions in joke structure, theories of how it produces humor, delivery features, exceptions (anti-jokes), and related narratological constructs (jab lines, three-part structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch line definition and function
rubrics_metrics.description: A punch line concludes a joke; it is intended to make people laugh. It is the third and final part of the typical joke structure, following the introductory framing and the narrative which sets up the punch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a broader sense, a punch line can refer to the unexpected and funny conclusion of any performance, situation, or story. Example: framing 'A man walks into a bar...', narrative 'he hurts his head', punch line 'It was an iron bar!'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script-based semantic mechanism (Raskin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is evoked when a trigger contained in the punch line causes the audience to abruptly shift its understanding of the story from the primary (more obvious) interpretation to a secondary, opposing interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To produce humor the two interpretations (scripts) need to be both compatible with the joke text and opposite or incompatible with each other; the punch line is the pivot signaling this shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage incongruity and resolution (Shultz)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor appreciation involves a biphasic sequence: first the discovery (perception) of incongruity, then the resolution of that incongruity. Incongruity alone is insufficient to account for humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within this framework, resolution of the incongruity is what generates laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosodic delivery markers are unreliable
rubrics_metrics.description: Folk theories claim punchlines are delivered louder, at a higher pitch, or with a dramatic pause, but laboratory findings show none of these changes are employed at a statistically significant level in production of humorous narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch and loudness of the punch line are comparable to the ending of any narrative (humorous or not); do not assume special prosodic cues are required for a successful punch line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch line placement: single end-of-story requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke contains a single story with a single punch line placed at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For longer humorous texts an expanded narratological model is needed; the classical expectation is a single concluding punch line per joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jab lines: internal humorous elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A jab line designates humor within the body of a text rather than at the end; jab lines are semantically identical to punch lines but can be positioned anywhere within the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jab lines are integrated into the narrative (not disruptive) and either indispensable to plot/text development or not antagonistic to it; useful when applying the GTVH to longer works (novels, sitcoms, plays, films).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-jokes and 'jokes without a punch line' (shaggy dog, nonsense)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some long-winded anti-jokes (shaggy dog stories) deliberately subvert expectation by being anticlimactic; nonsense jokes provide either no resolution or only a partial, unsatisfactory resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor in these forms often derives from fooling the audience into expecting a conventional punch line so the audience becomes the butt of the joke. Example: 'No soap, radio.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-part structure (AAB / rule of three)
rubrics_metrics.description: Felicitous jokes are often formatted as a set of three (AAB) where the first two share an attribute and the third deviates; that third item is the punch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes following the AAB structure are consistently rated funnier than AB or AAAB counterparts; the punch line functions as a deviation and its funniness does not depend on how many A instances precede it.
